findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise a SyntaxError when the view renders
findings.body: The closing tag of the if/else block is written as `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The compiled template becomes `... end if <buffer append>`, i.e. the stray `if` starts a new, never-closed conditional, so rendering `embed#best` raises a SyntaxError and every embed request for an already-imported topic returns a 500. Controller specs don't render views, so this is not caught by the added tests.

findings.title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into inline JavaScript (reflected XSS)
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates the *host* of the referer, so an attacker-controlled path/query such as `http://<embeddable_host>/x'+alert(document.cookie)+'` passes validation and breaks out of the string literal, executing arbitrary JS in the Discourse origin. Use `escape_javascript`/`j` and preferably pass only the scheme+host origin (which is all postMessage uses anyway).

findings.title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized remote HTML as `cooked`
findings.body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the markdown/sanitization pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `i.content` from an arbitrary remote RSS/Atom feed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with this cook method, so anything the feed publisher puts in the item body (`<script>`, event handlers, iframes) is rendered verbatim to every forum visitor — a stored XSS vector. Feed/imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (as `import_remote` does with its tag/attribute whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

findings.title: Feed items without `content` raise NoMethodError and abort the whole poll
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every item exposes `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Because the items are processed in a single `each` loop with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, one such item aborts the entire polling run and all remaining items are silently skipped. Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap per-item processing so one bad item cannot kill the job.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. Those are rewritten to `http://embedhost//cdn.example.com/img.png` (the `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips the leading slashes), producing broken links and broken images for any feed that uses protocol-relative references. Exclude hrefs/srcs starting with `//` before prefixing.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the throttle key exists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, so that embed URL can never be imported again (the embed page will loop on the loading template indefinitely). Use `SET key 1 EX 60 NX` (or `setex` guarded by existence) instead.

findings.title: `force: true` added to an already-released migration can drop an existing table
findings.body: This migration was already shipped; editing it to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that on any database where the migration is re-run (re-seeded schema, repaired schema_migrations, `db:migrate:redo`) the existing `top_topics` table is dropped along with its data instead of failing loudly. The change is also unrelated to the embedding feature in this PR and should be reverted.

findings.title: No test renders the embed views; assertions hidden in an `after` hook
findings.body: The specs never render the views (controller specs don't by default), which is why the syntax error in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%- end if %>`) goes undetected — the only new user-facing templates are completely untested. Additionally, `response.should be_success` and the X-Frame-Options assertion live in an `after` block: hook failures are reported detached from the example and run even when the example already failed, making diagnosis hard. Add a `render_views` request/controller spec for `embed#best` (both the loading and the topic-found paths).

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that happens to be a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For `discourseUrl = "http://forum.example.com/"`, an attacker-controlled frame on `http://forum.example.co` passes the check. Compare the origin for exact equality against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` instead, and ignore messages whose `source` is not the created iframe.

findings.title: Kernel#open used with externally supplied URLs (SSRF / command execution)
findings.body: `open(url).read` in `import_remote` and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed` use `Kernel#open`, which executes a shell command when the argument starts with `|` and happily fetches `file://` and internal addresses. The feed URL is a per-site setting (a site admin on a multisite install should not be able to run commands on the host), and `import_remote` is also invoked from the Disqus importer with URLs taken from the dump. Use `URI.parse(...).open`/`Net::HTTP` restricted to http(s), with a timeout.

findings.title: Existing embed with a deleted post crashes the import
findings.body: When a `TopicEmbed` row already exists, `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted or the association pointing at a missing row). The code then calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, raising NoMethodError inside the retrieval job/feed poll. Guard on `post.blank?` and either recreate the topic or skip.

findings.title: `import` mutates the caller's `contents` string
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the argument supplied by the caller rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or cache the content (and any frozen string passed in, which would raise) get surprising behaviour, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate multiple "Imported from" footers. Use `contents + ...` / `dup` instead.

findings.title: `feed_key` is dead code
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a `feed-modified:` Redis key but nothing in the class (or anywhere else in the PR) reads or writes it, so there is no conditional-GET/If-Modified-Since handling as the name implies. Either implement the caching it was intended for or remove the method so future readers don't assume polling is throttled.

findings.title: Loading page is cached for 1 minute while the page reloads every 30 seconds
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `loading` template, whose inline script reloads after 30s. The browser/proxy will serve the cached loading page for the first reload, so the user waits at least a minute even when the topic was imported quickly. Skip caching (or use a much shorter max-age) on the loading response.

findings.title: "ALLOWALL" is not a valid X-Frame-Options value
findings.body: `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` sets a non-standard token. Browsers that don't recognise it are entitled to fall back to denying framing, which would break embedding entirely. The reliable way to permit framing is to delete the header (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`), optionally alongside a CSP `frame-ancestors` entry for the embeddable host.

findings.title: embed_url limited to 255 characters with a unique index
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` creates a varchar(255). Article URLs with query strings/UTM parameters routinely exceed 255 characters, so those imports will fail with a value-too-long error (and the unique index on the column limits how long an indexable value can be). Consider `t.text` with an index on a hash/prefix, or document the limit and truncate/normalise the URL before insert.
